haiku-low.q1: At step 4, after lint passes and before any new instance starts, as a single one-off job. The live release must still work against the migrated schema.
haiku-low.q2: Never, through deploy migrations: lint rejects any migration that drops or renames a column or table.
haiku-low.q3: Pass the health gate (4 instances, 3 passes in a row each) and the smoke suite within 10 minutes of first start. Otherwise abort (step 8): new instances stopped, live colour kept.
haiku-low.q4: One API call changes the public listener's forward target from the old target group to the new one. No gradual shift.
haiku-low.q5: A judged 5-minute window above 1% 5xx after switch. Repoints listener to old group, stops new instances, records rollback. Migrations not reversed.
haiku-low.q6: Until T+30, the 30-minute rollback window. After teardown, a normal deploy of the previous release (steps 1 to 9) handles it.
haiku-low.q7: Earlier migrations stay, being additive; any failed index is dropped. Deploy stops; new release never starts; live colour keeps serving. Fix by new forward migration.
haiku-low.q8: Public listener's forward target, checked against 'live' in deploy state (AWS Parameter Store). Other colour is idle. Disagreement stops and alerts.
haiku-low.q9: Lock: CI group catalog-web-deploy, held from step 1 until watch ends at T+15 or abort; released before rollback window.
haiku-low.q10: A private test listener on the same ALB forwards to the idle target group, so smoke tests reach the new release while users cannot.
haiku-low.q11: CI runs them as a single one-off job before any new instance starts. The document does not say how once-only is enforced.
haiku-low.q12: Removed from the idle target group and stopped (abort), or stopped after repoint (rollback). Next deploy starts from a clean idle colour.

sonnet.q1: Step 4, after build and lint and before any new instance starts, run once as a single one-off job. The live (old) release must keep working on the migrated schema, since migrations are additive and it uses only things that already exist. After colour teardown, the previous release also still works.
sonnet.q2: NOT STATED as allowed. Migration lint rejects any migration that drops, renames, or changes the type of a column or table, so such changes cannot be deployed through this procedure. The document does not say when or how they could be done.
sonnet.q3: The new release must pass the health gate (all 4 instances pass /healthz 3 times in a row) and the full smoke suite, both within 10 minutes of the first instance starting. Otherwise (or on any smoke failure) it aborts at step 8: new instances are removed and stopped, the candidate is marked failed, the lock is released, the engineer is alerted, and users are never touched.
sonnet.q4: Step 9: one API call changes the public listener's forward target from the old target group to the new one. There is no gradual shift. It applies fully or not at all.
sonnet.q5: Any judged 5-minute window (at least 100 requests) with a 5xx share above 1% during the 15-minute watch after T. A rollback repoints the public listener to the old target group, stops the new colour's instances, makes the old colour live again, marks the candidate failed, clears the rollback target, and closes the window. Migrations are never reversed. A manual rollback in the window does the same.
sonnet.q6: 30 minutes after the switch (until T+30). Automatic rollback covers the first 15 minutes, and an engineer can start a manual rollback job from T+15 to T+30. After T+30 the old colour is torn down, so a problem is handled as a normal deploy of the previous release (steps 1 to 9); the older release works with the migrated schema because migrations are additive.
sonnet.q7: Migrations that already succeeded stay in place (they are additive, so safe). A failed concurrent index build is left INVALID, and the job drops it before exiting so the next run can rebuild it. The deploy stops at step 4: the new release is never started and the live colour keeps serving. Nothing is rolled back automatically. The fix is a new forward migration. The document does not describe what happens inside a partially applied single migration beyond the index case.
sonnet.q8: Step 2 reads the public listener's forward target and compares it with the live colour in deploy state. The colour the listener forwards to is live, the other is idle and gets the new release. If they disagree, or the idle colour still has running instances, the run stops and alerts. Deploy state is one record in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.
sonnet.q9: The lock, the CI concurrency group catalog-web-deploy (one holder at a time, others queue). A run holds it from step 1 until its watch ends (T+15) or it aborts. An automatic rollback releases it when done. It is released before the rollback window opens, and runs finding an open window release it and wait. Teardown and manual rollback jobs take it as well.
sonnet.q10: Through the test listener, a private second listener on the same ALB whose forward target is the idle target group. The public listener still forwards to the live (old) target group for users.
sonnet.q11: A single one-off job in step 4 runs all pending migrations. It runs once because it is one job per deploy, before any new instance starts, and the deploy holds the lock so only one run at a time. The document does not describe any other once-only mechanism.
sonnet.q12: After an abort (step 8) the 4 new instances are removed from the idle target group and stopped. After a rollback they are stopped, after the listener is repointed. Either way the idle colour is clean, so the next deploy starts from a clean idle colour. Step 2 stops the run if the idle colour still has running instances.
